claim: Google's 2004 S-1/A identifies PageRank, developed at Stanford, as one element of Google's web-page ranking technology and separately states that Stanford owns the PageRank patent licensed to Google.
notes: PageRank is one element among multiple ranking/search techniques; this does not support attributing all search or advertising value to the patent.

claim: By the 2004 S-1/A, Google reported indexing more than 4 billion web pages and described its search/advertising infrastructure as processing search activity at very large scale.
notes: Scale of the search value carrier; not a patent-level metric.

claim: Google reported total revenues of $1.465934 billion for 2003 and $1.351835 billion for the six months ended June 30, 2004.
notes: Enterprise-level realized value only. It must not be attributed to PageRank or US6285999.

claim: Google disclosed that it held a perpetual license to the Stanford-owned PageRank patent, with exclusivity extended through 2011 and the patent stated to expire in 2017.
metric_value: exclusive through 2011; perpetual license thereafter; patent stated to expire in 2017
notes: This is a rights-horizon fact, not a value amount.

claim: Google's 2008 Form 10-K again identifies PageRank as one element of the technology used to rank web pages and explains that it is combined with other ranking and text-matching techniques.
notes: Continued implementation does not imply that all Google search value is attributable to this single patent.

claim: Google reported total 2008 revenues of $21.79555 billion.
notes: Enterprise-level realized value only. It must not be attributed to PageRank or US6285999.

claim: Google disclosed that the Stanford-owned PageRank patent was licensed perpetually to Google, that exclusivity would continue only through 2011, and that the patent was stated to expire in 2017.
metric_value: exclusive through 2011; perpetual non-exclusive thereafter; patent stated to expire in 2017
notes: At the late T0, historical implementation is mature while the remaining exclusivity window is materially shorter than at the early T0.

claim: Google's 2008 Form 10-K describes web search operating at global scale, with access to billions of web pages and an interface available in 120 languages.
metric_value: billions of web pages; interface in 120 languages
notes: Product/platform-scale evidence only; it is not a patent-level value amount.
